sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: Cubism began in ______ in about 1907.
______ was the pioneer of Cubism.
Important Cubist artists were Picasso, Braque and ______.
The Cubists chose still life, landscapes and ______.
The Cubist movement came to an end by ______.

sections.passage: Cubism is a style of painting and sculpture that began in Paris in about 1907. It was the most important trend at the beginning of the 20th century. Cezanne was the pioneer of Cubism. He said, 'Everything in nature must be treated as a cylinder or sphere'. The important artists included Picasso, Braque and Leger. They chose subjects like still life, landscapes and portraits. The aim was to give importance to construction but not emotions. By 1920 this art movement came to an end. (October 2025)

questions.q: Surrealism started in ______.
Surrealists used the images of the ______.
Surrealism was influenced by ______.

Abstract art is ______ art.

sections.passage: Surrealism was another movement which started in 1924 and continued till 1955. The Surrealist artists tried to use the images of the unconscious in their works. They were mainly influenced by psycho-analysis. It originated as a revolutionary movement resulting from the Dadaists' revolt. Giorgio de Chirico and Salvador Dali were the most famous Surrealist painters. Abstract art is a general term for non-representational art; it started in 1910 and its pioneers were Kandinsky, Delaunay and Mondrian.

sections.title: Read the passage and state whether each statement is true or false.

questions.q: Any work which is representational is considered Abstract Art.
questions.answer: False – a non-representational work is Abstract Art.

questions.q: Picasso and Salvador Dali did not remain individualistic.
Cubism originated along the lines of Abstract Art.
The beginning of the phase of Abstract Art starts with the works of Kandinsky.

sections.passage: An important phase in Western art began with the foundation of Abstract Art. We find the influence of Abstract Art in works which cannot be related to realism. Any work which is non-representational is considered Abstract Art. Though Abstract Art, Cubism and Surrealism originated in the West, they left a deep impression on Indian artists. Wassily Kandinsky, Salvador Dali and Pablo Picasso represented important phases in these movements, but they remained very individualistic. Cubism originated along the lines of Abstract Art and Picasso became famous for his Cubist paintings and sculptures. Dali was the most famous amongst the Surrealist painters. The beginning of the phase of Abstract Art starts with the works of Wassily Kandinsky. (April 2025)

questions.q: Mention two of Picasso's famous periods.
questions.answer: The Blue Period (1900–02), named after the blue-green tone of his canvases, and the Rose Period (1905–07), in which he used mainly pink; also his Cubist phase, from which he became world famous.

questions.q: What do you mean by the term Cubism? Who are the artists who began this style?
questions.answer: Cubism is a style of painting and sculpture which began in Paris in about 1907, breaking three-dimensional forms into flat geometrical areas and showing parts from different viewpoints at once. Cezanne was its pioneer; Picasso, Braque and Leger were the important artists.

questions.q: Determine the style of the painting 'Man with Violin' and name the painter.
questions.answer: It is a fine example of Analytical Cubism, painted by Pablo Picasso in 1912.

questions.q: Name two famous painters of the Surrealism style.
questions.answer: Salvador Dali and Giorgio de Chirico.

questions.q: When did Wassily Kandinsky paint 'Black Lines'?
Write a short note on Abstract Art.
questions.answer: Abstract art is a general term for non-representational art that rejects realistic depiction of the world. It began about 1910 and its pioneers are Kandinsky, Delaunay and Mondrian, who gave pictured form to abstract ideas that cannot be shown realistically.

questions.q: Describe the painting 'Persistence of Memory'.
questions.answer: Salvador Dali painted it in 1931 (oil on canvas, Museum of Modern Art, New York). A bare, calm landscape holds melting clocks with ants crawling over a watch, expressing a disturbed mind and the world of dreams; the technique is realistic but the objects are out of place.

sections.title: Short answer question. Answer in 50–60 words.

questions.q: Give a note on the painting 'Black Lines' by Kandinsky.
questions.answer: 'Black Lines' (oil on canvas, December 1913, Guggenheim Museum, New York) is an abstract composition in which black paint lines in one corner take different meanings according to their arrangement, with coloured spots that look applied by the fingers of a giant hand. It shows simplicity and pure diagrams, like skeletons without flesh; line, shape and colour have their own meaning and the lines seem to have lives of their own.

questions.q: Briefly describe Salvador Dali's contribution to Surrealism.
questions.answer: Dali was the most famous Surrealist painter, a Spanish painter, film maker and writer. He used a highly realistic, academic and precise technique to depict the world of absurd, strange and dream-like elements and an unconventional grouping of objects with symbolic meaning. 'Persistence of Memory', 'Small Bottle of Rum' and 'Honey is Sweeter than Blood' are his works.

questions.q: Write in brief about Pablo Picasso.
questions.answer: Picasso (born 1881 in Malaga, Spain) was a painter, sculptor and ceramist who followed abstract composition. His Blue Period (1900–02) and Rose Period (1905–07) were followed by African influence and the Cubist phase, which made him world famous; 'Man with Violin' (1912) is analytical cubism; 'Guernica' shows the Spanish Civil War.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 70–80 words.

questions.q: What is Surrealism? Choose any one painting of Pablo Picasso and describe it.
questions.answer: Surrealism (1924–55) was a movement in which artists used images of the unconscious, influenced by psycho-analysis and arising from the Dadaists' revolt; Dali and de Chirico were the leading painters. Picasso's 'Man with Violin' (1912, oil on canvas, 100 x 73 cm, Philadelphia Museum of Art) is a fine example of Analytical Cubism: the man holding the violin is broken into geometrical shapes showing different viewpoints at once, in shades of brown and green, with unity of form and colour.

questions.q: What is analytical cubism? Describe a famous painting of this style.
questions.answer: Analytical Cubism divides an object into parts showing different viewpoints at the same time; forms are recognisable but broken into cube-like forms. 'Man with Violin' (Picasso, 1912) breaks the human form with the violin into geometrical shapes arranged together, painted in browns and greens with a continuous unity of form and colour.

questions.q: Define Cubism in art. Choose any painting of Kandinsky and describe it.
questions.answer: Cubism, begun in Paris about 1907 with Cezanne as pioneer and Picasso, Braque and Leger as artists, breaks forms into geometrical shapes and stresses construction, not emotion. Kandinsky's 'Black Lines' (1913, oil on canvas) is an abstract work of black lines and coloured spots in which line, shape and colour have their own meaning.
